topic: Design-based quadratic minimax frontier for interference specification tests. For fixed known minimum-degree-two repeated-motif graphs, iid Bernoulli(1/2) assignment, and bounded schedules y_i(z)=beta_i1+beta_i2z_i+beta_i3T_i(z), test H0:beta_i3=0 against spillover RMS rho. Optimize Q_w=n^-1sum_iw_i(T_i)Y_i^2, prove attainment and the correct conditional-variance Sion dual, and establish rho*=V_quad^1/4 up to constants with exact worst-null calibration and an all-test converse. Gao et al. arXiv:2605.09726 own the estimator and upper bound; Tiwari--Basu arXiv:2608.22890 own validity and simulations, not local minimax power. Consumer: LinkedIn's Bernoulli feed-ranking arm. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The moment equations make Q exactly unbiased for rho^2 because Z_i is independent of T_i. Finite-dimensional coercivity follows from sparse legal baseline schedules, so Sion applies to integral Var_Z(Q_w|beta)dPi, not mixture-law variance. For disjoint triangles, w=(8,-8,8); enumeration gives Var(Q)=64/n at beta_i1=1 and the bounded-outcome envelope gives V_quad<=192/n. The null f_a versus alternative f_(aT_i) construction factors conditional on assignment; h0 proportional to cos^8 has boundary order eight, symmetric shifts cancel first order, and direct analysis numerically supports H^2(f_a,f_(at))<=Ca^4 uniformly. Searches found no matching local minimax theorem and repo neighbors target estimation, ambiguity, or confidence intervals. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform shifted-support Hellinger lemma and convert its product bound into the composite all-test lower bound with constants matching the repeated-motif V_quad comparison. EARLY KILL TEST: First formalize the Hellinger bound, Sion compactification, and complete triangle enumeration; pivot or stop if Hellinger is quadratic, the dual requires variance under a mixed observation law, or the triangle scale fails.

open_problems.open_problem: Can an assignment-ancillarity-preserving least-favorable subexperiment on repeated motifs yield a uniform fourth-order shifted-support Hellinger bound and a composite all-test lower bound at the quadratic fourth-root frontier?

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs an unbiased estimator of squared spillover magnitude and an upper bound but explicitly does not pursue tight rates or a matching all-test converse.
source_refs.author: Chao Gao, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes design-based validity and simulation power while leaving theoretical power under restricted alternatives unresolved.
source_refs.author: Supriya Tiwari and Pallavi Basu

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies design-based Le Cam mixture lower bounds for estimation under interference, but not a fourth-order local testing converse.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, and Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.excerpt: exact homogeneous-witness transport that attains the effective rare-exposure count
preserves all assignment ancillaries and arbitrary external interval randomization

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gao et al. provide the quadratic upper-bound mechanism but no matching converse, while Tiwari–Basu identify theoretical local power as missing. Prior CausalSmith constructions show how to transport homogeneous witnesses and reconstruct discarded assignments so arbitrary randomized procedures cannot exploit ancillaries. The missing step is specific: compactly supported translated laws can have one-sided or infinite KL divergence, and the desired fourth-root boundary requires a squared-Hellinger bound of order a^4 uniformly over legal baseline shifts. That motifwise bound must then tensorize and be converted into a lower bound for the composite null against all measurable tests, with constants comparable to the optimized conditional variance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform one-motif inequality H^2(P_a,P_{a,t}) <= C a^4 over every legal baseline shift, followed by an exact product-experiment reduction and a Le Cam or Bayes theorem showing that every level-alpha test has bounded power when rho <= c V_quad^(1/4).

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from unrestricted impossibility to a structured quadratic estimator supplies the closest motivation and problem formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exposure-model specification is generally untestable -> structured network-linear alternatives make squared spillover estimable -> an upper bound alone does not identify the detection limit -> build a bounded repeated-motif hard experiment and prove the all-test frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its design-based Le Cam reduction and mixtures over deterministic potential-outcome schedules, evaluating closeness conditional on assignment before averaging over the known design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest all-procedure lower-bound framework preserving fixed potential outcomes and assignment ancillaries; the new proof must upgrade its affinity calculation to fourth order.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the quadratic-functional testing mixture and cancellation argument producing the regular n^(-1/4) separation regime.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Testing whether a nonnegative quadratic functional vanishes has the same fourth-root geometry, with design variance over repeated motifs replacing regression-noise variance.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the attained conditional-variance minimax dual and complete minimizing-weight set for unbiased quadratic spillover statistics on a fixed repeated motif?

source_refs.claim: The proposed statistic uses one feasible Riesz weight and a deliberately crude covariance bound; optimality, attainment, and tight graph-specific variance are not established.
source_refs.author: Chao Gao, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: The design-based Riesz framework characterizes unbiased linear estimation but does not solve the worst-schedule variance geometry of quadratic functionals.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.excerpt: neither determines this finite-block minimax constant or the complete minimizing local-weight set.
Sharpen the OEQ by proposing a candidate finite-block symmetrization or convex-duality route for the exact constant

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing moment equations establish feasibility, not optimality. The legal weights form a finite-dimensional affine space, whereas the adversary ranges over bounded baseline, direct-effect, and spillover schedules coupled through the motif. The earlier SNIPE representer program is linear in outcomes, but the present null variance is quartic in nuisance schedules. Moreover, replacing sup_beta Var_Z(Q_w|beta) by variance under a mixture over beta adds a between-schedule term and therefore produces the wrong game. The missing proof must establish coercivity or compactify the weight space and apply minimax duality to the integral of assignment-conditional variances.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An attained equality inf_w sup_beta Var_Z(Q_w|beta) = sup_Pi inf_w integral Var_Z(Q_w|beta)dPi(beta), together with a finite convex or semidefinite representation, the exact value for disjoint triangles, and necessary-and-sufficient conditions for every minimizing weight.

writing_exemplar.why: Its quadratic statistic and acknowledged loose variance analysis define the precise destination problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Structured spillovers admit an unbiased quadratic moment -> one feasible weight proves consistency -> nuisance schedules determine its dispersion -> solve the exact motifwise conditional-variance game and characterize all optimal weights

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-induced inner products and Riesz representers to parameterize the affine class of unbiased weights, then replace minimum L2 norm by worst-schedule conditional variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unbiasedness constraints are finite exposure-space orthogonality equations; the desired theorem begins exactly where representer existence ends.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain its exposure-moment reproduction equations while replacing covariance envelopes by exact motif enumeration and convex maximization over bounded schedules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its statistic has the identical observation-level form Q_w = n^(-1) sum_i w_i(T_i)Y_i^2.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a full-sample quadratic statistic be calibrated at exact finite-sample level against the composite no-spillover null with arbitrary bounded unit-specific baselines and direct effects while retaining fourth-root local power?

source_refs.claim: Exact p-values for nonsharp interference hypotheses are obtained through artificial experiments restricted to focal units and assignments where the null becomes sharp.
source_refs.author: Susan Athey, Dean Eckles, and Guido W. Imbens
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The conditioning-mechanism framework obtains valid randomization tests under interference by restricting the randomization distribution to imputable outcomes.
source_refs.author: Guillaume W. Basse, Avi Feller, and Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: Conditional randomization tests for exposure specifications require careful focal-unit and focal-assignment choices because the null is nonsharp.
source_refs.author: Tadao Hoshino and Takahide Yanagi

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes asymptotic design-based validity and simulation power, not exact worst-null finite-sample calibration with a local minimax guarantee.
source_refs.author: Supriya Tiwari and Pallavi Basu

open_problems.why_unsolved: No interference is a nonsharp null because only one of each unit's two own-treatment potential outcomes is observed. Existing exact tests restore imputability by conditioning on focal units or assignments, thereby discarding information, while asymptotic specification tests do not give exact worst-null control. Exact unbiasedness of Q_w does not identify its finite-sample null law: calibration requires maximizing the rejection probability over all bounded nuisance schedules. It remains unknown whether this optimization has a tractable extremal solution whose conservatism still permits power at the V_quad^(1/4) scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable critical value or randomized rejection rule satisfying sup_beta:H0 P_Z(reject) <= alpha for every finite repeated-motif graph and bounded null schedule, together with a power theorem above C V_quad^(1/4).

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly frames exposure specification as a nonsharp-null problem and explains why exact inference ordinarily uses focal conditioning.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exposure mappings define spillover estimands -> their specification nulls are nonsharp -> conditioning restores exact imputability but sacrifices observations or assignments -> obtain exact composite-null calibration without abandoning the full-sample quadratic signal

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the artificial-experiment proof of exact validity as the benchmark against which nuisance-maximized full-sample calibration must be established.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical finite-sample exact test for a nonsharp no-spillover hypothesis on a network.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the conditioning-mechanism formalism to isolate what assignment conditioning proves and what must instead be controlled through least-favorable nuisance optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its theorem pinpoints the exact-validity obstacle caused by unavailable counterfactual outcomes under a composite interference null.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit the quadratic weight's annihilation of baseline and direct-effect moments to derive an extremal null calibration sharper than a moment-inequality threshold.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The statistic's orthogonal moment structure offers the most direct possible route to full-sample exact calibration.

open_problems.open_problem: For Bernoulli assignment on disjoint copies of a fixed interference motif, is the all-test invariant minimax game attained by a quadratic statistic Q_w, or can a nonquadratic invariant test achieve strictly better worst-case local power?

source_refs.excerpt: A pair-preserving symmetry reduction with a joint assignment--observation coefficient yields an exact finite conic game

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior construction solves an estimation game after quotienting paired schedules by a permutation group. The interference test instead has overlapping exposures, squared outcomes, composite-null nuisance coefficients, and an RMS-separated alternative. Its assignment-marked coefficient recursion therefore must be replaced by null and alternative experiment kernels and a testing-affinity dual. Until that finite invariant experiment is derived, a lower bound matching Q_w proves only its rate optimality and cannot establish exact quadratic completeness or rule out a nonquadratic constant-factor improvement.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite-dimensional primal-dual characterization of invariant tests on one motif, a tensorization theorem across motif copies, and either equality with the optimized Q_w minimax value or a finite rational certificate that a nonquadratic invariant test is strictly better.

writing_exemplar.why: Its valid quadratic procedure naturally motivates asking whether restriction to quadratic tests loses minimax power.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A computable quadratic spillover test is available -> validity and an upper bound do not prove procedural optimality -> quotient the repeated-motif experiment -> compare Q_w with every invariant measurable test

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over mixed-strategy minimax geometry and contact-certificate arguments to the finite invariant testing game.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution requires optimizing over randomized procedures and certifying a saddle-point face, structurally matching finite minimax experimental-design geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its unrestricted-procedure minimax reduction and least-favorable finite-population schedules from squared-error estimation to testing affinity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest design-based template for comparing a restricted procedure class with an all-measurable-procedure benchmark under interference.

literature_map:
Gao, Harshaw, Sävje, and Wang (2026, arXiv:2605.09726) prove unrestricted exposure-model specification testing impossible and construct a quadratic Riesz estimator for squared spillover under a scalar linear-in-means alternative; tight variance rates remain open.
Tiwari and Basu (2026, arXiv:2608.22890) develop an asymptotically valid design-based specification test and simulations while identifying theoretical power, restricted alternatives, basis choice, and dense graphs as unresolved.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) develop graph-dependent design-based minimax estimation theory and Le Cam mixtures over deterministic schedules, but not local minimax specification testing.
Hoshino and Yanagi (2026, Journal of Applied Econometrics, DOI 10.1002/jae.70076; earlier arXiv:2301.05580) give conditional randomization tests for hierarchical exposure specifications and sequential FDR control.
Athey, Eckles, and Imbens (2018, JASA, arXiv:1506.02084) obtain exact p-values for nonsharp network hypotheses through artificial experiments on focal units and assignments.
Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019, Biometrika, arXiv:1709.08036) formalize conditioning mechanisms for valid randomization tests under interference, with power tied to retained assignment variation.
Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1910.10862) encode imputability as bicliques and analyze conditional-test power without deriving an all-test local minimax radius.
Pouget-Abadie et al. (2019, Biometrika, arXiv:1704.01190) design a Hausman-style interference test and demonstrate it on LinkedIn feed ranking, providing the closest application anchor.
Aronow (2012, Sociological Methods & Research, DOI 10.1177/0049124111432535) gives foundational randomization inference under interference but no quadratic specification-testing frontier.
Basse and Airoldi (2018, Sociological Methodology, DOI 10.1177/0081175018782569) show that unbiasedness under parametric interference need not imply decreasing design variance.
Zhong (2024, arXiv:2409.12496) studies minimax network experiments for global treatment effects, emphasizing design-dependent information rather than specification-test power.
Zng, Imai, and Jiang (2025, arXiv:2503.11358) study design-based inference testing under general interference but do not identify this repeated-motif fourth-root frontier.
Comminges and Dalalyan (2013, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/13-EJS766) establish sharp minimax testing rates for quadratic functionals, including the regular n^(-1/4) regime.
The live tension is therefore between available unbiased quadratic upper bounds and exact-validity frameworks on one side, and the missing conditional-variance dual, fourth-order affinity lemma, and all-test local converse on the other.
